image.prompt: Create an extraordinarily realistic outdoor photograph, the opening view of a first-person mountain hike, absolutely photographic not an illustration or game render. Camera at standing eye height 1.7m, wide 26mm natural lens. A narrow warm sandy switchback footpath starts at bottom center, curls gently right through lush green montane forest and climbs uphill toward a sunlit rocky overlook in the middle distance. Large textured living Jeffrey pine trunks frame both edges, mature irregular pine branches overhead, rich emerald and fresh lime green foliage, delicate ferns and golden grasses beside the trail, a few purple lupines and yellow wildflowers, uneven granite rocks embedded naturally in the soil. On the left about 10 meters away a realistic mule deer quietly grazes among plants, small in the composition, natural accurate anatomy, not facing the camera. In the far distance between trees is a breathtaking Sierra Nevada granite mountain range and a deep forested valley under a bright blue sky with thin white clouds. A warm clear spring morning, sunlight from upper left makes realistic dappled shadows. Complex actual forest ecology, rich detail, believable atmosphere, inviting and colorful but natural. Foreground fully in focus; beautiful distant aerial perspective. No people, no text, no branding, no signs, no overlays, no lens flare, no oversaturation, no fantasy. The trail and the distant overlook are part of a single continuous walkable landscape. Composition suitable as the beginning of an interactive cinematic journey for a school hiking club.

sequence.prompt: ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS UNBROKEN FIRST-PERSON WALK, no cuts, no edits, no transitions, no montage. Starting exactly from the supplied forest photograph, the camera physically walks forward at steady human walking speed along this SAME sandy footpath for the full 12 seconds, about 16 meters total. Camera remains at human eye height 1.7m above the actual ground at every point, never flies. The camera follows the visible gently curving path uphill and slightly right. Immediate foreground pine trunks, fern leaves, flowers, and rocks pass to either side with convincing three dimensional parallax. The same small mule deer from the image briefly raises its head naturally on the left while continuing to graze, anatomically correct. Branches sway very slightly in a light breeze. Everything stays geographically stable and realistic. The distant granite Sierra Nevada mountains remain the SAME mountains for the entire shot, slowly becoming unobstructed as the walker passes the last nearby trees and approaches the sunlit rocky overlook. For the final 2 seconds the walk gently settles at the overlook, still at walking height on the granite ledge: magnificent uninterrupted panoramic view of the same forest valley and rugged mountain range, vibrant green trees on the slopes, bright blue sky and thin wispy clouds. This is real outdoor landscape documentary photography, not game graphics, no CGI appearance. Bright inviting spring morning, beautiful realistic warm sunlight and richly detailed natural colors. No people, no hands, no text, no signs, no overlays, no voice or music, no fades, no dissolves, absolutely NO scene change, NO jump cut, NO morphing. Stable smooth gimbal walk with almost no head bob. The physical continuous walking journey is the entire purpose of the shot.

delivery: 241 individually addressable WebP frames, 20 samples per source second. Only user scroll selects displayed frames. No autoplay or video element. The camera path is fixed.
review: Visually inspected source contact sheet at one-second intervals. FFmpeg scene threshold 0.24 detected no abrupt scene cuts.
disclosure: Generated landscape and wildlife. Not a documented club outing or a verified real trail.
